class.name: Activity
class.brief_description: A full-screen UI screen with an Android-style lifecycle.
class.description:
Activity is the base class for every screen in a game_framework application. Each Activity is driven by [ActivityManager], which calls the [code]dispatch_*[/code] lifecycle methods — users override the virtual [code]_on_*[/code] callbacks in GDScript instead.
Lifecycle order: - On launch: [method _on_create] → [method _on_start] → [method _on_resume] - On navigate away: [method _on_pause] → [method _on_stop] (may be [method _on_destroy] if removed from stack) - On return: [method _on_resume] (from stopped state) - On finish: [method _on_pause] → [method _on_stop] → [method _on_destroy]
Activity holds a [Context] reference and re-exports the most common Context methods directly, so you can write [code]start_activity(it)[/code] instead of [code]get_context().start_activity(it)[/code].
[b]Implementation note.[/b] Activity is a C++ [code]IContext[/code] via the [code]ContextBase[/code] CRTP mixin — at the C++ level, it [i]is[/i] a Context. The convenience methods (start_activity / show_toast / get_service / load_resource_*) are inherited, not duplicated. GDScript binding names are 100% backward compatible. Internally Activity holds an [code]Application *[/code] rather than the abstract [code]Context *[/code]: [method get_context] returns this Application (upcast to Context, since Application IS-A Context), and the legacy [method set_context] is preserved as an alias that down-casts to Application.
[b]Run-As-Standalone (Strategy).[/b] When an Activity scene is opened directly in the editor (F6 / "Play Scene") without an [ActivityManager] hosting it, the Activity's [member launcher] decides whether to self-host. The default launcher is [StandaloneActivityLauncher], which spawns a minimal [Application] + [code]StandaloneRoot[/code] under [SceneTree.root], reparents the Activity, and drives the GDScript lifecycle. To disable the bootstrap, set [code]launcher = null[/code] or assign a custom launcher. Override [method _on_setup_standalone] to register mock services before [method _on_create] fires.
[b]Run-As-Standalone[/b] When an Activity scene is opened directly (e.g. F6 / "Play Scene" in the editor, or [code]godot --path . <activity>.tscn[/code] on the command line) without an [ActivityManager] hosting it, the Activity bootstraps a minimal [Application] automatically: - A new [Application] node and a [code]StandaloneRoot[/code] full-screen Control are spawned under the scene tree root. - The Activity is reparented under [code]StandaloneRoot[/code] so [Dialog] / [Toast] layering matches the managed path. - It is added to the Activity stack (so [method back] / [method finish] work normally) and [code]finish()[/code] on the last standalone Activity calls [SceneTree.quit]. - [b]No[/b] services are pre-registered. Override [method _on_setup_standalone] to register mock services or pre-load data. - To suppress the bootstrap, set [member launcher] to [code]null[/code], or swap to a custom [ActivityLauncher] subclass.

method.name: _on_back_pressed
method.description: Called when the system back gesture is triggered. Return [code]true[/code] to consume the event (prevent default close behavior), or [code]false[/code] to let [ActivityManager] finish this Activity. Default returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: _on_create
method.description: Called once when the Activity is created, before it becomes visible. [param saved_state] is currently an empty Dictionary (state save/restore is not yet implemented); pass data via [member Intent.extras] instead. This is where you build the UI tree, create the [ViewModel], and set up bindings.

method.name: _on_destroy
method.description: Called when the Activity is being permanently destroyed. Release resources, dispose the [ViewModel], etc. After this callback the node will be removed from the scene tree.

method.name: _on_new_intent
method.description: Called when the Activity is reused via [code]FLAG_SINGLE_TOP[/code], [code]FLAG_CLEAR_TOP[/code], or [code]FLAG_REORDER_TO_FRONT[/code] — instead of creating a new instance, the existing one receives the new [Intent].

method.name: _on_pause
method.description: Called when the Activity is no longer the active (focused) screen. A new Activity is being started on top, or this one is being finished.

method.name: _on_resume
method.description: Called when the Activity becomes the active (focused) screen. Either the initial launch after [method _on_start], or returning from a covered state.

method.name: _on_setup_standalone
method.description: Called only on the Run-As-Standalone bootstrap path, right after the host [Application] is built but before [method _on_create]. Override this to register mock services, preset Intent extras, or seed any resource the Activity expects when ActivityManager would normally have wired them up. Not called when the Activity is opened via [method Context.start_activity].

method.name: _on_start
method.description: Called after [method _on_create], when the Activity becomes visible for the first time. The UI tree is already in the scene.

method.name: _on_stop
method.description: Called when the Activity is fully hidden (covered by a new Activity that finished its enter transition). The node is still in the scene tree but [member CanvasItem.visible] is set to [code]false[/code].

method.name: back
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.back]. Triggers the system back gesture: calls [method _on_back_pressed] on the current top Activity; if not consumed, finishes it.

method.name: finish
method.description: Requests the ActivityManager to finish (destroy) this Activity. Lifecycle: pauses, stops, destroys, then auto-dismisses owned Dialogs, cancels owned Toasts, and runs the exit transition.

method.name: finish_top
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.finish_top]. Finishes the current top Activity.

method.name: get_application
method.description: Returns the [Application] hosting this Activity. Equivalent to [code]get_context()[/code] but typed as [Application] for convenience. Returns [code]null[/code] before the Activity has been wired up (e.g. during [code]_init[/code]).

method.name: get_context
method.description: Returns the [Context] assigned to this Activity. The context provides access to Application-wide services (navigation, resource loading, service discovery, etc.).

method.name: get_intent
method.description: Returns the [Intent] that was used to launch this Activity.

method.name: get_no_history
method.description: Returns whether this Activity was launched with [code]FLAG_NO_HISTORY[/code]. When [code]true[/code], the Activity is automatically destroyed when navigating away from it, instead of being kept in the back stack.

method.name: is_standalone
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this Activity was promoted by the Run-As-Standalone bootstrap (i.e. it is the entry scene and built its own [Application]). Returns [code]false[/code] when it was driven by an existing [ActivityManager].

method.name: get_resource_handle
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.get_resource_handle].

method.name: get_service
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.get_service].

method.name: has_service
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.has_service].

method.name: load_resource_async
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.load_resource_async].

method.name: load_resource_sync
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.load_resource_sync].

method.name: set_application
method.description: Sets the [Application] hosting this Activity. Called automatically by [ActivityManager] during activity creation, or by the Run-As-Standalone bootstrap. Most users do not need to call this directly. Calling [method set_context] with an Application also works (it is a backward-compat alias).

method.name: set_no_history
method.description: Sets whether this Activity stays in the back stack. Set by [ActivityManager] when launched with [code]FLAG_NO_HISTORY[/code].

method.name: show_dialog
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.show_dialog]. The Dialog's lifecycle owner is set to this Activity — it will be auto-dismissed when this Activity is destroyed.

method.name: show_toast
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.show_toast]. The Toast's lifecycle owner is set to this Activity — it will be cancelled when this Activity is destroyed.

method.name: start_activity
method.description: Convenience for [method Context.start_activity].

members.member: The startup strategy invoked on [code]NOTIFICATION_READY[/code]. Default = [StandaloneActivityLauncher] (enables the F6 single-Activity debug workflow). Set to [code]null[/code] to disable any auto-launch, or assign a custom subclass for editor-preview / nested-activity / multi-window setups.
If [code]true[/code], this Activity will be destroyed when a new Activity is started on top of it, instead of being paused and kept in the back stack.
The [Transition] resource used when this Activity enters the screen.
The [Transition] resource used when this Activity exits the screen.
